2.2.4 A Maximum of Storage Capacity for CO2 with SO2

For impurities which have higher critical temperature than that of CO2, no storage capacity minimum would occur in the corresponding CO2 mixture. Rather, a maximum can appear based on an analysis similar to that for the non-condensable impurities. This has been verified with calculated results for the CO2 mixture with 2.9 vol % SO2 (the Cansolv® absorption system case presented in the previous IEA GIG report PI14/32). As shown in Figure 2.6, a maximum is seen at about 11 MPa, where the storage capacity is increased by over 5%. It should be noted again that the storage capacity is based on pure CO2 (see discussion for Equation 2.5). It is, therefore, interesting to see that in this peak region, the CO-based capacity is above that of pure CO2. In other words, SO2 does not take any but creates space for CO2. This can be rationalized from the consideration that SO decreases average distance between the molecules of the mixture - an opposite effect of that of the non-condensable gases. This can be taken as one positive effect of the presence of SO on CO2 storage. However, SO2 causes more concern with regard to its chemical effects on formation rocks. This will be discussed later.
